# Exercise - Simple randomization

A small trial compares treatments `A` and `B`. The trial uses simple randomization with equal allocation.

## Exercise 1

Generate one randomization list for `n = 20` patients using `randomizr::simple_ra()`. How many patients are allocated to each treatment? What is the final absolute imbalance `|n_A - n_B|`?



```{r}

set.seed(101)
trt <- randomizr::simple_ra(N = 20, conditions = c("A", "B"))
trt

table(trt)
abs(sum(trt == "A") - sum(trt == "B"))
```


## Exercise 2

Repeat the same trial 2000 times and estimate the probability that the final imbalance is at least 6 patients.


```{r}
set.seed(102)
nsim <- 2000
n <- 20

prob_ge6 <- mean(replicate(nsim, {
  trt <- randomizr::simple_ra(N = n, conditions = c("A", "B"))
  abs(sum(trt == "A") - sum(trt == "B")) >= 6
}))

prob_ge6
```


## Exercise 3

Repeat the simulation for `n = 20`, `n = 50`, and `n = 100`. Compare how often an imbalance of at least 6 patients occurs. What do you conclude about simple randomization in small and large trials?



```{r}
set.seed(103)
nsim <- 2000

prob_ge6 <- function(n) {
  mean(replicate(nsim, {
    trt <- randomizr::simple_ra(N = n, conditions = c("A", "B"))
    abs(sum(trt == "A") - sum(trt == "B")) >= 6
  }))
}

res <- sapply(c(20, 50, 100), prob_ge6)
res
```
